mainTopic: Teachings about creation: אדם הראשון's size, the first-day creations and light, the qualities of creation, and the order of heaven and earth
overview: The גמרא learns from a פסוק in דברים that אדם הראשון was created enormous, reaching the sky and spanning the world, which is one and the same size, and that God made him smaller after he sinned. רב then lists ten things created on the first day, gives a פסוק for each, and a ברייתא explains what תהו and בהו are. The גמרא asks how light can be a first-day creation when the lights were placed in the sky on the fourth day. רבי אלעזר answers that the first-day light was a special far-seeing light that ה׳ hid for the צדיקים, while חכמים say the sun and moon were made on day one and only hung on day four. רב also lists ten qualities through which the world was created, and teaches that the world and the sea kept spreading until ה׳ rebuked them; ריש לקיש reads the name שדי as 'the One who said enough.' בית שמאי, בית הלל and חכמים argue whether heaven or earth came first, and ריש לקיש settles the clashing פסוקים with two stages. The amud ends with explanations of the word שמים and with רבי עקיבא explaining why the first פסוק says את before heaven and earth.

steps.title: Why do we need the phrase about the day God created man?
steps.stepSummary: Since the limits of inquiry are already learned from 'למקצה השמים', the phrase 'למן היום אשר ברא אלהים אדם על הארץ' seems extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that we learn the rule from 'from one end of the heavens to the other end of the heavens,' why do I need 'since the day that God created man upon the earth'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that one phrase of the פסוק seems unnecessary and asks what it comes to teach. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier teaching already used 'למקצה השמים ועד קצה השמים' to mark the limits of what a person may ask about. So the earlier phrase 'למן היום' looks like it adds nothing. The גמרא assumes every phrase in the תורה must teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that it is derived (we already learn it from somewhere)
Why do I need it? (asking what an extra phrase teaches)

phrases.english: Now that it is derived
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier teaching about which questions on creation a person may ask.

phrases.english: from "from one end of the heavens to the other end of the heavens,"
"since the day that God created
man upon the earth"
— why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of how the פסוק in דברים sets limits on studying creation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the phrase 'למן היום אשר ברא אלהים אדם על הארץ' teach, if the limits are already learned from another phrase?

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: אדם הראשון reached from the earth to the sky
steps.stepSummary: The phrase teaches the teaching of רבי אלעזר: אדם הראשון reached from the earth to the sky, and after he sinned הקדוש ברוך הוא made him smaller.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for the teaching of רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר said: אדם הראשון reached from the earth up to the sky, as it says, 'Since the day that God created man upon the earth.' Once he sinned, הקדוש ברוך הוא placed His hands on him and made him smaller, as it says, 'Behind and before You formed me, and You placed Your palm upon me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'extra' phrase teaches something new: how tall אדם הראשון was when he was created. It also explains what happened to his size after the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אדם על הארץ' are read as describing אדם הראשון himself: a man standing on the earth who reached the sky. A second פסוק from תהלים, 'You placed Your palm upon me,' shows that God pressed him down and made him smaller after he sinned. So the phrase is not extra after all.

keyTerms.meaning: According to (the teaching of) רבי אלעזר

phrases.english: It is needed for the teaching of Rabbi Elazar.
For Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן מִן הָאָרֶץ עַד לָרָקִיעַ,
phrases.english: Adam the first man reached from the earth to the sky,
as it is stated: "Since the day

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים אָדָם עַל הָאָרֶץ״.
phrases.english: that God created man upon the earth."
phrases.notes: He reads it as: the man was standing on the earth, and the next words say how far up he reached.

phrases.english: And once he sinned —

phrases.aramaic: הִנִּיחַ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יָדָיו עָלָיו וּמִיעֲטוֹ,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, placed His hands upon him and made him smaller,
as it is stated: "Behind and before You formed me,
and You placed Your palm upon me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 by giving the phrase a new teaching.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase teaches that אדם הראשון reached from the earth to the sky, and that God made him smaller after he sinned.

steps.title: רב: אדם הראשון stretched from one end of the world to the other
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that אדם הראשון stretched across the whole world, learning it from 'from one end of the heavens to the other,' and that God made him smaller after he sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: אדם הראשון stretched from one end of the world to the other, as it says, 'Since the day that God created man upon the earth, and from one end of the heavens to the other end of the heavens.' Once he sinned, הקדוש ברוך הוא placed His hand on him and made him smaller, as it says, 'And You placed Your palm upon me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching about אדם הראשון's size, from רב. רב measures אדם הראשון along the length of the world instead of up to the sky.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads the whole פסוק together: the man created on the earth stretched 'from one end of the heavens to the other.' That describes a sideways measure across the world. Like רבי אלעזר, he says God made אדם הראשון smaller after the sin, using the same פסוק from תהלים.

keyTerms.meaning: From one end of the world to its other end

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן, מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ הָיָה,
phrases.english: Adam the first man stretched from one end of the world to its other end,
as it is stated: "Since the day that
God created man upon the earth,
and from one end of the heavens to the other end of the heavens,"
once he sinned,

phrases.aramaic: הִנִּיחַ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יָדוֹ עָלָיו וּמִיעֲטוֹ,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, placed His hand upon him and made him smaller,
as it is stated: "And You placed Your palm upon me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second description of Adam's size, using the next phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדם הראשון stretched from one end of the world to the other, and God made him smaller after the sin.

steps.title: The two phrases seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: If one phrase says Adam reached the sky and the other says he stretched across the world, the phrases seem to give two different sizes.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the phrases contradict each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts the two teachings side by side and asks how they can both be true. This challenge sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's phrase gives a height, from the earth to the sky. רב's phrase gives a width, from one end of the world to the other. Since both phrases are in the same פסוק describing the same man, it looks like they give two different measurements.

phrases.english: If so, the phrases contradict each other!
phrases.notes: He means the two parts of the פסוק: 'upon the earth' (up to the sky) and 'one end of the heavens to the other' (across the world).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the combination of steps 2 and 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two readings of the פסוק about Adam's size.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One phrase measures Adam's height to the sky and the other measures his width across the world, so the פסוק seems to give two different sizes.

steps.title: Both distances are the same size
steps.stepSummary: The distance from the earth to the sky equals the distance from one end of the world to the other, so both phrases describe the same size.
steps.simpleTranslation: This and that are one measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no contradiction: the height up to the sky and the width across the world are the same distance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that height and width meant two different sizes. The answer shows they are equal, so the two phrases simply describe the same size in two directions. רבי אלעזר and רב therefore do not disagree.
steps.whatToRemember: אדם הראשון was created enormous, reaching the sky and spanning the world, which is one and the same size. After the sin, הקדוש ברוך הוא made him smaller.

phrases.english: This and that are one measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the two measurements are actually equal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Earth-to-sky and end-to-end of the world are two different sizes, so the phrases conflict.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both distances are the same, so the phrases agree and both teachings stand.

steps.title: Ten things were created on the first day
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: ten things were created on the first day: heaven and earth, תהו and בהו, light and darkness, wind and water, and the length of day and of night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Ten things were created on the first day. They are: heaven and earth, תהו and בהו, light and darkness, wind and water, and the length of day and the length of night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רב listing ten things that were created on the very first day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the discussion of creation that began with אדם הראשון's size. The list comes in five pairs. Each pair will be backed by a פסוק in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The unformed and empty state of the world
The set length of day and of night

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Ten things were created on the first day,
and these are they:
heaven and earth, tohu and vohu,
light and darkness, wind and water,
the length of day and the length of night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new teaching from the same speaker, moving from אדם הראשון's size to the list of first-day creations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten things were created on the first day: heaven, earth, תהו, בהו, light, darkness, wind, water, the length of day and the length of night.

steps.title: A פסוק for each item on the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows where each of the ten things appears in the first-day account in בראשית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Heaven and earth, as it says: 'In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.' תהו and בהו, as it says: 'And the earth was תהו and בהו.' Light and darkness: darkness, as it says: 'And darkness was on the face of the deep'; light, as it says: 'And God said: Let there be light.' Wind and water, as it says: 'And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the water.' The length of day and night, as it says: 'And there was evening and there was morning, one day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves each part of רב's list by pointing to a phrase in the first day's פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every item on the list shows up in the פסוקים before the words 'one day', so it must have been made on the first day. Darkness is proven before light because darkness appears first in the פסוקים. The day-and-night pair comes from 'evening and morning', which marks out how long each lasts.

phrases.english: Heaven and earth, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים אֵת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֵת הָאָרֶץ״,
phrases.english: “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth,”
Tohu and vohu, as it is written:
“And the earth was tohu and vohu,”
Light and darkness: darkness, as it is written:
“And darkness was on the face of the deep,”
Light, as it is written:
“And God said: Let there be light,”
Wind and water, as it is written:
“And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the water,”
The length of day and the length of night, as it is written:
“And there was evening and there was morning, one day.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק for each of the ten items רב listed.
steps.raayaObject: רב's list of ten things created on the first day
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוקים of the first day in בראשית 1:1-5

steps.title: What תהו and בהו really are
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that תהו is a green line around the whole world that darkness comes from, and בהו is wet stones sunk in the deep that water comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: תהו is a green line that surrounds the entire world, and darkness came out from it, as it says: 'He made darkness His hiding place all around Him.' בהו is damp stones sunk in the deep, and water comes out from them, as it says: 'And He will stretch over it the line of תהו and the stones of בהו.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains what the unclear words תהו and בהו mean, since they were on רב's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word is tied to something physical, and each is the source of another first-day item: תהו makes darkness and בהו makes water. The פסוק in ישעיהו proves that תהו is a 'line' and בהו is 'stones', because it uses those exact words together.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught:
Tohu is a green line
that surrounds the entire world,
from which darkness came out,
as it is said: “He made darkness His hiding place all around Him.”
Vohu: these are the damp stones
that are sunk in the deep,
from which water comes out,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְנָטָה עָלֶיהָ קַו תֹהוּ וְאַבְנֵי בֹהוּ״.
phrases.english: as it is said: “And He will stretch over it the line of tohu and the stones of vohu.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains two items from the list that are hard to understand.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תהו is a green line around the world that darkness comes from; בהו is wet stones in the deep that water comes from.

steps.title: Was light really created on the first day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: the פסוקים say the lights were put in the sky on the fourth day, so how can light be counted as a first-day creation?
steps.simpleTranslation: And was light created on the first day? But it is written: 'And God placed them in the sky of the heavens,' and it is written: 'And there was evening and there was morning, a fourth day'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question against רב's list: light seems to have been made on the fourth day, not the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sun and moon, the sources of light, are set in the sky in the fourth day's account. That seems to clash with counting light among the first day's ten things. The next step answers this.
steps.confusionAlert: Both 'evening and morning' פסוקים look alike. Step 7 used the one ending 'one day'; here the גמרא uses the one ending 'a fourth day'.

phrases.english: And was light created on the first day?
But isn't it written: “And God placed them in the sky of the heavens,”
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:17. 'Them' means the sun, moon and stars.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וַיְהִי עֶרֶב וַיְהִי בֹקֶר יוֹם רְבִיעִי״!
phrases.english: and it is written: “And there was evening and there was morning, a fourth day”!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks one item, light, from רב's list and its proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that light was created on the first day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים place the lights in the sky on the fourth day, which suggests light came into being then and not on day one.

steps.title: The first-day light was a special light that ה׳ hid
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי אלעזר, the light of day one was not sunlight. It was a special light for seeing across the whole world, and ה׳ hid it because of the wicked generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי אלעזר, who said: the light ה׳ created on the first day let a person see from one end of the world to the other. When ה׳ saw that the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion acted wickedly, He hid that light from them, as the פסוק says: 'And from the wicked their light is withheld.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 9. The light of day one is a different light from the sun and moon of day four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that 'light' means the sun and moon, which were placed on day four. רבי אלעזר says the first-day light was a separate, special light, so there is no contradiction. The פסוק from איוב is brought to show that a light was held back from the wicked.

keyTerms.meaning: the generation of the Flood (in the time of נח)
the generation of the Dispersion (the builders of the Tower of בבל)
He hid it away, stored it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of light. The first-day light here is NOT the sun. It is a special light that was hidden. The sun and moon are the 'lights' hung on day four.

phrases.english: It is in line with Rabbi Elazar.
For Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹר שֶׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: The light that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created on the first day,

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם צוֹפֶה בּוֹ מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ.
phrases.english: a person could see by it from one end of the world to the other.
Once the Holy One, Blessed be He, looked
at the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion
phrases.notes: The 'Dispersion' is the generation of the Tower of בבל, which ה׳ scattered across the world.

phrases.english: and saw that their deeds were corrupt,
He arose and hid it from them,
as it is said: "And from the wicked their light is withheld."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9 by redefining the first-day 'light'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition: the first-day light is a different, special light, not the sun and moon
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'light' of day one is the sun and moon, which were only placed on day four, so רב is wrong to count it on day one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first-day light was a special far-seeing light, later hidden, so רב correctly counts it as a first-day creation.

steps.title: The hidden light is saved for the righteous
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר continues: the light was saved for the צדיקים in the future, and the light itself was happy about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For whom did ה׳ hide it? For the צדיקים in the time to come. The פסוק says 'God saw the light, that it was good,' and 'good' means a צדיק, as it says 'Say of the righteous that it is good.' When the light saw that it was saved for the צדיקים, it rejoiced, as it says 'The light of the righteous will rejoice.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר keeps going and explains who the hidden light was saved for. He brings פסוקים to back each point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'כי טוב' in בראשית as a hint to צדיקים, because elsewhere a צדיק is called 'טוב'. That links the first-day light to the righteous. The last פסוק is read to mean that the light itself rejoices at being saved for them.

keyTerms.meaning: in the time to come, the future world
good; here a hint to a צדיק

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, the first-day light was a special light. ה׳ hid it from the wicked and saved it for the צדיקים in the future.

phrases.english: And for whom did He hide it?
For the righteous in the time to come,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב״,
phrases.english: as it is said: "And God saw the light, that it was good,"
and "good" means nothing other than a righteous person,
as it is said: "Say of the righteous that he is good."
When the light saw that He had hidden it for the righteous,
it rejoiced,
as it is said: "The light of the righteous will rejoice."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אלעזר's statement from Step 10, adding where the hidden light went.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The hidden first-day light is stored for the צדיקים in the future, and the light rejoices in this.

steps.title: A dispute of תנאים: רבי יעקב's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this question is a dispute between תנאים. רבי יעקב holds like רבי אלעזר that the first-day light was a special far-seeing light.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים: The light ה׳ created on the first day let a person look and gaze from one end of the world to the other. These are the words of רבי יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the same issue was already argued about by תנאים. Here it brings the first side, רבי יעקב, and sets up the other side, חכמים, in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב's words match רבי אלעזר almost exactly. This shows that the answer in Step 10 has an earlier source among the תנאים.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute between תנאים:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹר שֶׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: The light that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created on the first day,
a person could look and gaze by it
from one end of the world to the other;
these are the words of Rabbi Yaakov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי אלעזר's answer in Step 10 matches the view of the תנא רבי יעקב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יעקב: the first-day light was a special light by which one could see across the whole world.

steps.title: חכמים: the sun and moon were made on day one but hung on day four
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree. The first-day light was the sun and moon themselves. They were created on day one and only set in place in the sky on day four.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: These are the very same lights that were created on the first day, but they were not hung up in the sky until the fourth day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the other side of the dispute. חכמים give a different way to answer the question from Step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים do not need a special hidden light. In their view, the sun and moon really were created on day one, which fits רב's list. Day four is only when they were placed in their spots in the sky.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain why light counts as a first-day creation. רבי יעקב, like רבי אלעזר, says it was a special light by which one could see across the whole world, and רבי אלעזר adds that ה׳ hid it. חכמים say the sun and moon were created on day one and only hung up on day four.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both views keep רב's list of first-day creations correct. They just explain the day-four פסוקים differently.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: הֵן הֵן מְאוֹרוֹת שֶׁנִּבְרְאוּ בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: These are the very same lights that were created on the first day,
but they were not hung up until the fourth day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing תנאים view to רבי יעקב in Step 12, which offers a second answer to Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: the sun and moon were created on day one and were only placed in the sky on day four.

steps.title: The world was created through ten qualities
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטרא בר טוביה, quoting רב, lists ten qualities through which ה׳ created the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב: The world was created through ten things: wisdom, understanding, knowledge, strength, rebuke, might, righteousness, justice, kindness and mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching starts. רב gives a list of ten qualities that ה׳ used when He created the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא was discussing what was created on the first day. Now it moves to how the world was created. The list is stated here, and the next step will bring a פסוק for each item.

keyTerms.meaning: Rebuke, a sharp command to stop

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Zutra bar Tuvya said that Rav said:
The world was created through ten things:
through wisdom, through understanding, and through knowledge,
and through strength, through rebuke, and through might,
through righteousness and through justice, through kindness and through mercy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the first-day light dispute to a new teaching about the qualities used in creation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world was created through ten qualities: wisdom, understanding, knowledge, strength, rebuke, might, righteousness, justice, kindness and mercy.

steps.title: A פסוק for each of the ten qualities
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק for each pair or item in רב's list, showing that each quality appears in פסוקים about creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wisdom and understanding: 'ה׳ founded the earth with wisdom, He set up the heavens with understanding.' Knowledge: 'By His knowledge the depths were split.' Strength and might: 'He sets the mountains firm with His strength, He is wrapped in might.' Rebuke: 'The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at His rebuke.' Righteousness and justice: 'Righteousness and justice are the base of Your throne.' Kindness and mercy: 'Remember Your mercies, ה׳, and Your kindnesses, for they are from long ago.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through רב's list and gives a פסוק as the source for each quality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק links a quality to building the world: the earth, the depths, the mountains or the heavens. The last פסוק says mercy and kindness are 'from long ago,' meaning they were there from the start of the world. The פסוק about rebuke will be used again in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: From long ago, from the beginning

phrases.english: Through wisdom and through understanding, as it is written:
"ה׳ founded the earth with wisdom,
He established the heavens with understanding."
Through knowledge, as it is written:
"By His knowledge the depths were split open."
Through strength and might, as it is written:
"He sets the mountains firm with His strength, He is wrapped in might."
Through rebuke, as it is written:
"The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at His rebuke."
Through righteousness and justice, as it is written:
"Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne."
Through kindness and mercy, as it is written:
"Remember Your mercies, ה׳, and Your kindnesses,
for they are from times of old."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source in the פסוקים for each item in רב's list.
steps.raayaObject: רב's list of ten qualities used in creation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: פסוקים from משלי, תהלים and איוב that link each quality to forming the world.

steps.title: The world kept stretching until ה׳ rebuked it
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that when the world was created it kept expanding, like thread unrolling from balls of yarn, until ה׳ rebuked it and made it stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: When ה׳ created the world, it kept spreading out like two balls of weaving thread unrolling, until ה׳ rebuked it and made it stand still, as it says: 'The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at His rebuke.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a second teaching about creation. The world kept growing bigger until ה׳ ordered it to stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains what the 'rebuke' in creation was: a command that stopped the world from growing. The same פסוק from איוב that was the source for 'rebuke' in the last step is used here as proof. The 'pillars of heaven' trembling shows the world being forced to stand still.

keyTerms.meaning: Balls of thread used for the long threads in weaving
And He made it stand still

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת הָעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: When the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world,
it kept on expanding
like two balls of warp thread,
phrases.notes: Picture two balls of yarn rolling apart, with the thread between them getting longer and longer.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁגָּעַר בּוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְהֶעֱמִידוֹ,
phrases.english: until the Holy One, Blessed be He, rebuked it and made it stand still,
as it is stated: "The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at His rebuke."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on 'rebuke' from the list and explains what it did in creation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world kept expanding at creation until ה׳ rebuked it and stopped it.

steps.title: שַׁדַּי means 'the One who said enough'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב's teaching matches ריש לקיש's reading of the name אֵל שַׁדַּי: ה׳ is the One who told the world 'enough.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what ריש לקיש said: What does the פסוק 'I am אֵל שַׁדַּי' mean? It means: I am the One who said to the world 'enough.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects רב's teaching to another teaching that says the same idea, a reading of ה׳'s name שַׁדַּי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads שַׁדַּי as two parts: שֶׁ ('who') and דַּי ('enough'). That matches רב's teaching that ה׳ stopped the world from stretching further. The word וְהַיְינוּ tells us the גמרא is showing that two teachings agree.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same as

phrases.english: And this is what Reish Lakish said:
What is the meaning of what is written: "I am El Shaddai"?
I am the One who said to the world, "Enough."
phrases.notes: He reads שַׁדַּי as שֶׁ־דַּי, 'who said enough.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that ריש לקיש's reading of שַׁדַּי says the same thing as רב's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name שַׁדַּי means ה׳ is the One who told the world 'enough' and stopped it from expanding.

steps.title: The sea kept spreading until ה׳ rebuked it
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches the same idea about the sea: it kept spreading until ה׳ rebuked it and dried it up.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: When ה׳ created the sea, it kept spreading out, until ה׳ rebuked it and dried it, as it says: 'He rebukes the sea and dries it, and makes all the rivers dry.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a similar teaching. This time it is about the sea instead of the whole world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as רב's teaching: something keeps growing until ה׳'s rebuke stops it. Here the rebuke dries the sea. The proof is a פסוק from נחום that uses the word for rebuke about the sea.

keyTerms.meaning: Dried up, made into dry land

steps.whatToRemember: Rebuke in creation means ה׳ setting a limit: the world and the sea would have kept spreading until ה׳ told them to stop.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת הַיָּם
phrases.english: When the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the sea,
it kept on expanding,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁגָּעַר בּוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְיִבְּשׁוֹ,
phrases.english: until the Holy One, Blessed be He, rebuked it and dried it up,
as it is stated: "He rebukes the sea and dries it up,
and He dries up all the rivers."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same idea of an expanding creation stopped by ה׳'s rebuke to the sea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sea kept expanding at creation until ה׳ rebuked it and dried it up.

steps.title: בית שמאי: heaven was created first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings a dispute about the order of creation. בית שמאי say heaven came first and earth after, based on the first פסוק of the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: בית שמאי say: Heaven was created first and afterward the earth was created, as it says: 'In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: which was created first, heaven or earth? בית שמאי say heaven, because the תורה's first פסוק names heaven before earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי learn the order of creation from the order of the words in the פסוק. This is only the first side of the dispute. The next step brings בית הלל's opposite view.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught, which introduces a ברייתא

phrases.english: The Sages taught: Beit Shammai say:
The heavens were created first
and afterward the earth was created,
as it is stated: "In the beginning God created
the heavens and the earth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic within מעשה בראשית: the order in which heaven and earth were created.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, heaven was created before the earth.

steps.title: בית הלל: earth was created first
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל disagree and say the earth came first, based on a פסוק that names earth before heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: The earth was created first and afterward heaven, as it says: 'On the day ה׳ God made earth and heaven.'
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל give the opposite view. Earth came first, because a different פסוק names earth before heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same method: the word order in a פסוק shows the order of creation. They just use different פסוקים that list the two in opposite orders. So now each side has a פסוק that seems to go against the other side.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that heaven and earth were both created at the start. The only question is which one came first.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
The earth was created first
and afterward the heavens,
as it is stated: "On the day that ה׳ God made
phrases.notes: בראשית ב:ד. In this פסוק earth comes before heaven.

phrases.english: earth and heaven."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to בית שמאי, using a פסוק with the reverse word order.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, the earth was created before heaven.

steps.title: בית הלל mock the idea of building the upper floor first
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל challenge בית שמאי: nobody builds the second floor before the house, and the פסוק calls heaven the upper floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: By your view, does a person build the upper floor first and only then the house? The פסוק calls heaven ה׳'s upper chambers and says His vault is founded on the earth.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל attack בית שמאי's view that heaven came first. They use a picture from everyday building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עמוס describes heaven as the upper story and earth as the foundation. A foundation always comes before an upper floor, so earth must have come first. This argues from common sense, backed up by a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: According to your words (by your own view)
An upper floor, a second story
His vault, the bundled structure He set on the earth

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:
According to your words,
does a person build an upper floor
and only afterward build the house?!
As it says: "He Who builds His upper chambers in the heavens
phrases.notes: עמוס 9:6. The פסוק calls heaven the 'upper chambers,' so heaven is the second floor.

phrases.english: and has founded His vault upon the earth."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי: לְדִבְרֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: בית הלל go on the attack after stating their own view in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's view that heaven was created first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Heaven is the upper floor, and you cannot build an upper floor before the house beneath it.

steps.title: בית שמאי mock the idea of making the footstool first
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer back: nobody makes a footstool before the chair, and the פסוק calls heaven the throne and earth the footstool.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to בית הלל: By your view, does a person make a footstool first and only then the chair? The פסוק says: The heavens are My throne and the earth My footstool.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי hit back with a picture of their own. You make the chair first and the footstool after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישעיהו calls heaven the chair and earth the footstool. The main item, the chair, gets made before its small accessory, so heaven came first. Each side has a פסוק and a common-sense picture, so neither side wins yet.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְבֵית הִלֵּל:
phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel:
According to your words,
does a person make a footstool
and only afterward make a chair?!
As it says: "So said ה׳:
The heavens are My throne, and the earth is My footstool."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְבֵית הִלֵּל: לְדִבְרֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A counter-attack against בית הלל's view, built the same way as step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's view that earth was created first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Heaven is the chair and earth the footstool, and nobody makes the footstool before the chair.

steps.title: The Sages say heaven and earth were created together
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים take a third view: heaven and earth were created at the same moment, based on the word יחדו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Sages say: Both were created as one, as it says: My hand founded the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens. I call to them and they stand together.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion enters. The חכמים say neither came first, because they were created at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the word יחדו, 'together,' in ישעיהו. The חכמים read it as describing the moment of creation: when ה׳ called them, they came into being together.

keyTerms.meaning: As one, at the same time

phrases.english: But the Sages say:
this and that were created as one,
as it says: "Indeed, My hand founded the earth,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 48:13. Watch for the last word, יחדו; that is the proof.

phrases.english: and My right hand spread out the heavens;
I call to them, they stand together."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: זֶה וָזֶה כְּאַחַת נִבְרְאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two sides cancel each other out, a third opinion offers a middle position.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven and earth were created at the same time.

steps.title: How do בית שמאי and בית הלל read the word 'together'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what בית שמאי and בית הלל do with the word יחדו, since they hold that one came before the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the others, what do they do with 'together'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the other two opinions deal with the חכמים' proof word. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יחדו really means 'created at the same time,' it would refute both בית שמאי and בית הלל. So they must read it some other way.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other(s), the opposing opinion(s)

phrases.english: And the others,
phrases.notes: He means בית שמאי and בית הלל, who don't agree with the חכמים.

phrases.english: what do they do with "together"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the proof word the חכמים used in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word יחדו means according to בית שמאי and בית הלל

steps.title: 'Together' means they never separate
steps.stepSummary: יחדו does not describe when they were created. It means heaven and earth stay attached and never pull apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means they do not pull apart from each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the others read יחדו as describing how heaven and earth stay connected, not when they were made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word moves from 'time of creation' to 'lasting connection.' Read that way, the פסוק says nothing about which came first, so בית שמאי and בית הלל keep their views.

keyTerms.meaning: They slip away or pull apart

phrases.english: That they do not pull apart from each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יחדו means heaven and earth remain joined and never separate, not that they were created at the same moment.

steps.title: The verses contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the פסוקים clash: some put heaven first and some put earth first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verses contradict each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a problem. The פסוקים each side quoted point in opposite directions, so we need a way to make them all true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion relied on a פסוק, and both sets of פסוקים are true. One order seems to cancel the other, so the גמרא needs one explanation that fits all of them.

phrases.english: The verses contradict each other!
phrases.notes: The first פסוק of the תורה names heaven first, while בית הלל's פסוק names earth first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the debate to point out the underlying clash between the פסוקים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוקים that list heaven and earth in different orders
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one פסוק says heaven came first and another says earth came first, they cannot both be literally right.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: heaven created first, earth spread out first
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש solves the clash by splitting creation into two stages: heaven was created first, but earth was spread out first.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: When they were created, He created heaven and afterward the earth. When He spread them out, He spread out the earth and afterward heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the contradiction. Each order is true, but about a different stage of creation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stage one is bringing them into being, and there heaven came first. Stage two is stretching them out into their final shape and place, and there earth came first. The פסוקים that put heaven first describe stage one, and those that put earth first describe stage two.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's two stages: heaven was created first, but earth was spread out first. That is how both sets of פסוקים can be true.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
When they were created,

phrases.aramaic: בָּרָא שָׁמַיִם וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּרָא הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: He created heaven and afterward created the earth,
and when He spread them out,

phrases.aramaic: נָטָה הָאָרֶץ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָטָה שָׁמַיִם.
phrases.english: He spread out the earth and afterward spread out heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two stages (creation and spreading out)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים seemed to describe one event in two opposite orders.
steps.terutzMaskana: Heaven was created first, but earth was spread out first. Each פסוק describes a different stage.

steps.title: What does the word שמים mean?
steps.stepSummary: Since the topic is heaven, the גמרא asks what the word שמים means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'heaven'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a side topic about the word שמים. This question sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not part of the order-of-creation debate. The גמרא is curious about where the name שמים comes from.

phrases.english: What is "heaven"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question prompted by the discussion of heaven.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning behind the word שמים

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר חנינא: 'there is water there'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא reads שמים as שם מים, 'water is there.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: The word means 'that there is water there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer reads the word שמים as two words joined together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שם (there) plus מים (water) sounds like שמים. So the name says that heaven is a place where water is found.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
That there is water there.
phrases.notes: A play on sounds: שם (there) plus מים (water) makes שמים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא: שֶׁשָּׁם מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמים means שם מים, 'water is there.'

steps.title: A ברייתא: heaven is made of fire and water
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads שמים as אש ומים: ה׳ mixed fire and water and made the sky from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: Fire and water. This teaches that the Holy One brought them, mixed them together, and made the sky out of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A second explanation of שמים, this time from a ברייתא. It sees two elements inside the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אש (fire) plus מים (water) sounds like שמים. This explanation goes further than step 29: the word tells us what the sky is made of, two opposites that ה׳ blended into one.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Fire and water,
phrases.notes: Another sound play: אש (fire) plus מים (water) makes שמים.

phrases.english: this teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, brought them
and mixed them with each other,
and made the sky from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different explanation of the word, from a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמים means אש ומים: the sky was made from fire and water mixed together.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל asks about the word את in the first פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל asks רבי עקיבא, who served נחום איש גם זו, what his teacher learned from the word את before heaven and earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל asked רבי עקיבא while they were walking on the road: You served נחום איש גם זו for twenty-two years, and he found a lesson in every את in the תורה. What did he learn from 'את the heaven and את the earth'?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. רבי ישמעאל asks רבי עקיבא what lesson the extra word את teaches in the first פסוק of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחום איש גם זו held that every את in the תורה adds something. In בראשית 1:1, though, it is hard to see what את could add to heaven and earth. Since רבי עקיבא learned from נחום for so long, רבי ישמעאל expects him to know.

keyTerms.meaning: You served (as a student who attends his teacher)
נחום of Gam Zu, רבי עקיבא's teacher
The occurrences of the word את

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאַל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אֶת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael asked Rabbi Akiva
when they were walking along the road,
he said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה שֶׁשִּׁימַּשְׁתָּ אֶת נַחוּם אִישׁ גַּם זוֹ
phrases.english: You who served Nachum of Gam Zu
for twenty-two years,
who used to expound every "et" in the Torah,
phrases.notes: את is a tiny word that points to the object of a verb. נחום found an extra lesson in each one.

phrases.english: "et the heaven and et the earth"
what would he expound from them?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאַל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אֶת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about the wording of the first פסוק of the תורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the word את teaches in 'את השמים ואת הארץ'

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: את shows that heaven and earth are real created things
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that without את, one might read שמים and ארץ as names of ה׳. The את makes clear they are the actual heaven and earth that were created.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it had said just 'heaven and earth,' I would have said 'heaven' is a name of the Holy One. Now that it says 'את the heaven and את the earth,' heaven means actual heaven and earth means actual earth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא explains that the את is needed to keep us from a dangerous misreading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without את, 'בראשית ברא אלקים שמים וארץ' could be read as if שמים and ארץ were names of whoever did the creating, alongside אלקים. The word את marks heaven and earth as the things that were created. So here the את does not add anything new; it keeps the meaning clear.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי עקיבא is learning an extra object from את here, the way נחום usually did. In this פסוק the את simply guards against reading heaven and earth as names of ה׳.
steps.whatToRemember: The את in the first פסוק makes clear that heaven and earth are things ה׳ created, not names of ה׳.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Had it said "heaven and earth" (without et),
I would have said:
"Heaven" is the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He.
phrases.notes: As if the פסוק were telling us who did the creating, instead of what was created.

phrases.english: Now that it says "et the heaven and et the earth,"
"heaven" means actual heaven,
"earth" means actual earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא answers רבי ישמעאל's question from step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The את prevents reading שמים and ארץ as names of ה׳ and shows they are the actual created heaven and earth.
